headline: OpenAI preps on-prem AI product with strict deletion terms
summary: New service terms reveal OpenAI is preparing to offer AI models for local deployment, but with mandatory deletion upon contract termination.
details: OpenAI has updated its Service Terms to include a new section on "Licensed Materials," which covers software delivered for installation on customer-owned systems, including local machines and private clouds. This move suggests the company is preparing to offer on-premises deployment options for its AI models.

The new terms specify that customers must permanently delete all copies of the "Licensed Materials" once their contract for the service ends. This clause is a significant detail for businesses considering local AI deployments, as it outlines a clear exit strategy and potential cost for integration.

Contract language for on-premises delivery often precedes the actual product launch. The inclusion of these terms signals a potential new direction for OpenAI, catering to businesses that require local deployment for security-sensitive work or data privacy reasons.

The license for these "Licensed Materials" is defined as limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, and non-sublicensable, with no rights for modification or redistribution. This ensures that the core AI models remain under OpenAI's control.

headline: Meta's Edits app gets AI assistant and desktop version to rival CapCut
summary: Meta's video-editing app Edits is expanding with an AI assistant for content ideas and a desktop version, aiming to boost creator engagement and compete with CapCut.
details: Meta is enhancing its video-editing app Edits with a new AI assistant and a desktop version, aiming to attract and retain creators. The AI assistant will analyze user insights to suggest content ideas and leverage trending audio, while the desktop version offers more precise editing control on a larger screen.

The AI assistant integrates directly with Instagram data, including views and retention insights, to help creators understand performance and brainstorm effective content. This move seeks to keep creators within Meta's ecosystem, reducing their reliance on external tools like ChatGPT for content strategy.

The desktop version of Edits is designed to offer creators more precise control and a better editing experience, especially for complex workflows. Meta emphasizes seamless syncing between mobile and desktop, directly challenging CapCut, which already provides a desktop application.

Alongside these upcoming features, Meta is rolling out a 'Beta' tab today, giving creators early access to experimental features and a platform for feedback. This initiative aims to accelerate development based on user needs and enhance Meta's competitive edge.

Additionally, Edits will now offer more detailed audience metrics, including demographic breakdowns and peak engagement times. These new analytics complement existing data on video watch duration, follower gains, and viewer drop-off points.

Content created with Edits reportedly sees a 10% higher save rate and a 2% higher reshare rate compared to content made elsewhere. Meta also states that over half of Reels viewers encounter Edits-created content daily.

While the AI assistant is currently in testing, the desktop version is slated for a "coming soon" release. Other features, including the Beta tab and expanded audience insights, are available starting today.
